nodes.description: The post-translational glycosylation carried out by the STT3B complex is dysfunctional, producing a glycosylation defect demonstrable across several substrates including GLUT1 and SHBG, and detectable clinically as abnormal serum transferrin glycosylation. Glycoproteomics shows the affected glycoprotein set is restricted rather than global — an important qualification when reusing the generic CDG module.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in MAGT1 lead to a glycosylation disorder with a variable phenotype.
evidence.snippet: All three patients have an N-glycosylation defect, as was shown by the study of different substrates, such as GLUT1 and SHBG, demonstrating that the posttranslational glycosylation carried out by the STT3B complex is dysfunctional in all three patients.

evidence.reference_title: Defective glycosylation and multisystem abnormalities characterize the primary immunodeficiency XMEN disease.
evidence.snippet: We also performed glycoproteomics analysis on T lymphocytes and show that XMEN disease is a congenital disorder of glycosylation that affects a restricted subset of glycoproteins.

nodes.description: Loss of NKG2D-dependent cytotoxicity leaves EBV-infected B cells inadequately controlled. EBV-associated B cell lymphoproliferative disease and lymphoma are the commonest causes of morbidity and mortality. Notably, EBV-naive children have a similar immunophenotype to EBV-positive patients, so the immune lesion precedes and is independent of infection.

evidence.reference_title: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Study of Magnesium Supplementation in Patients with XMEN Disease.
evidence.snippet: EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disease (LPD) and lymphoma are the most common cause of morbidity and mortality but EBV-naïve children have a similar immunophenotype to EBV+ patients

nodes.description: Loss-of-function mutation of the X-linked MAGT1 gene removes a subunit of the STT3B oligosaccharyltransferase complex, the machinery that performs post-translational N-glycosylation. TUSC3, the MAGT1 homolog, is upregulated, which may partially compensate. Note that MAGT1 is a non-catalytic subunit, so the annotation here is the decrease in the N-glycosylation process rather than loss of a catalytic molecular function; GO:0008250 (oligosaccharyltransferase complex) names the complex MAGT1 belongs to but is a cellular component and is not a valid MolecularFunctionTerm.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in MAGT1 lead to a glycosylation disorder with a variable phenotype.
evidence.snippet: MAGT1 has been described to be a subunit of the oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex and more specifically of the STT3B complex.

nodes.description: The wider phenotype attributable to hypoglycosylation of client glycoproteins beyond the immune compartment: lymphadenopathy, cytopenias, liver disease, cavum septum pellucidum, and — in patients ascertained by transferrin screening rather than by infection — intellectual and developmental disability as the dominant presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Defective glycosylation and multisystem abnormalities characterize the primary immunodeficiency XMEN disease.
evidence.snippet: We observed lymphadenopathy (LAD), cytopenias, liver disease, cavum septum pellucidum (CSP), and increased CD4-CD8-B220-TCRαβ+ T cells (αβDNTs), in addition to the previously described features of an inverted CD4/CD8 ratio, CD4+ T lymphocytopenia, increased B cells, dysgammaglobulinemia, and decreased expression of the natural killer group 2, member D (NKG2D) receptor.

nodes.description: NKG2D, the activating receptor encoded by KLRK1, is underglycosylated at a defined site in MAGT1-deficient patients, and its steady-state surface expression on CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes and NK cells is consequently lost. NKG2D is the best characterized but not the only affected client: glycoproteomic work describes a restricted set of hypoglycosylated immune glycoproteins also including CD28, HLA-DR beta and the T cell receptor alpha chain. Those additional substrates are stated in prose only, without an evidence block, because the cited abstracts here support the "restricted subset" claim generically rather than naming them. NKG2D and CD70 are required for control of Epstein-Barr virus, so this is the proximate immunological lesion. Critically, this step is a glycosylation defect and not a magnesium-signalling defect: magnesium neither restores NKG2D expression nor rescues the hypoglycosylation.
nodes.id: NKG2D Hypoglycosylation and Loss from Cytotoxic Lymphocytes

evidence.reference_title: Lack of NKG2D in MAGT1-deficient patients is caused by hypoglycosylation.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that the reduced steady-state levels of NKG2D are caused by hypoglycosylation of the protein and we pinpoint the exact site that is underglycosylated in MAGT1-deficient patients.

evidence.reference_title: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Study of Magnesium Supplementation in Patients with XMEN Disease.
evidence.snippet: Invariably, XMEN patients have decreased surface expression of the activating receptor “natural killer group 2D” (NKG2D) on CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL) and natural killer (NK) cells
